paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
model_annotation: The donut chart illustrates the distribution of samples (%) across two dimensions of ambiguity: sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring, labeled “Ambiguity Std (Outer),” is divided into four segments corresponding to standard deviation values of 0.0 (49.0%, dark blue), 0.47 (38.0%, medium blue), 0.82 (7.0%, light blue), and 0.94 (5.0%, very light blue). The inner ring, labeled “Max Ambiguity (Inner),” consists of three segments representing maximum ambiguity values of 1 (39.0%, medium-light blue), 2 (47.7%, medium blue), and 3 (14.2%, lightest blue). The chart visually aligns the inner and outer segments radially, allowing comparison of how each sample’s maximum ambiguity relates to its ambiguity standard deviation. Together, the rings indicate that most samples fall into the lower ranges of both ambiguity metrics, with nearly half showing no variation in ambiguity (Std: 0.0) and nearly half exhibiting a maximum ambiguity of 2. The legend on the right clarifies the color coding for both rings, and percentage labels are displayed directly on each segment for clarity.
